{{Quote|Baji is my name<br />From the planet Moltok I came.|[[Baji]]|<ref name="LCOJ">''[[The Lost City of the Jedi]]''.</ref>}}
'''Moltok''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Atrivis sector/Legends|Atrivis sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. [[Orbit/Legends|Orbiting]] close to its [[Star/Legends|sun]], the planet was quite warm, kept habitable only by the shielding action of active volcanoes. Beneath the ash they spewed forth, moist rain-forests covered the planet, home to a countless array of plant [[Species/Legends|species]]. The planet was home to two [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species, the [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]] and the [[Makurth/Legends|Makurth]]. The former were known throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for their botanical skills, while the latter often found employment as bodyguards in the criminal underworld.

The planet was part of galactic society from at least [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], with its natives participating in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], [[Mandalorian Wars]] and the [[New Sith Wars]]. Moltok almost faced ecological disaster in [[300 BBY/Legends|300 BBY]] when the Ho'Din began clearing large swaths of land for new industry. That led to a plague that could have spelled the extinction of the Ho'Din, had they not created a herbal remedy.

==Description==
Moltok was one of the inner [[Planet/Legends|planets]] of the [[Dartibek system]]<ref name="GG4" /> located within the [[Atrivis sector/Legends|Atrivis sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="SWR" /> It had such a swift [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] that on a planet of its proximity to a [[Star/Legends|star]], the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheric]] temperatures would typically be intolerable for life; however, Moltok had a number of active volcanoes that spewed ash into its skies. That layer of ash shielded the planet from a portion of the heat, bringing its temperatures within a comfortable range. The ash also caused diffraction at dawn and dusk, creating brilliant shades of [[Color/Legends|crimson]] in the sky. In the lower latitudes of the planet, the temperature reached up to 113 [[Standard (temperature)|standard degrees]] during the day. There were occasional cold spells on Moltok, which caused the reptilian [[Species/Legends|species]] on the planet to enter hibernation, and Moltok had such a high degree of axial tilt that the polar regions of the planet were significantly cooler than equatorial regions and inhospitable to the [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]].<ref name="GG4" />

The [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]]-rich world was covered in rain-forests of huge [[Tree/Legends|trees]], within which varying amounts of light produced distinct ecological layers. In the upper levels grew leafy greens&mdash;a staple diet for the native Ho'Din&mdash;and huge aerial vines that the arboreal sentients fashioned into walkways and structural supports. Enormous flowers up to several meters across also grew in that level, ranging in coloration from dark black to pale pink. On lower levels of the forests grew carnivorous plants, which were used by the Ho'Din as sentries to control [[Insect/Legends|insects]] and pests. Further down, the forest floor of Moltok teemed with organisms specializing in the breakdown of decaying matter. That activity replenished the soil, ensuring that the huge trees had adequate nourishment. Specific plants that grew on Moltok included the [[wuppa]]&mdash;its giant flowers of red and violet were reminiscent of Ho'Din tresses<ref name="GG4" />&mdash;and the [[Camba-Fruit]].<ref name="COJ" />

==History==
Two reptilian sentient species evolved on Moltok: the [[Makurth/Legends|Makurth]]<ref name="CCG" /> and the Ho'Din.<ref name="UAA" /> The space surrounding Moltok became integrated into the [[The galaxy/Legends|greater galaxy]] at some point between [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000]] and [[8000 BBY]],<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> with the Ho'Din active in galactic society from as early as [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], when [[Lohjoy]] served as an engineer for the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]].<ref name="Precipice">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]''.</ref> Later, members of the Ho'Din also served the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], as in [[3964 BBY]], when [[Oojoh]] trained as a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] on the Outer Rim world [[Taris/Legends|Taris]],<ref name="Kotor">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Commencement]]''.</ref> and [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Rutu]] served in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] during the [[Mandalorian Wars]].<ref name="AL">{{KOTORbackups|13}}</ref> Around [[3630 BBY]],<ref name="TOR dates">{{TOR_updates|5.0}}</ref> a long-abandoned city was discovered in Moltok's forests, and the settlement was investigated by explorers shortly before it was buried under ash from nearby volcanoes.<ref name="KOTET">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=crewskill|Archaeology|Underneath a Burning Sky}}</ref> Makurth were found offworld by [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] when at least one participated in the [[New Sith Wars]] on the side of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]],<ref name="DB">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''.</ref> despite Moltok owing its alleigance to the Republic. Thoroughout that period from 5000 to 1000 BBY, Moltok was a stopping point on a [[Coruscant–Dantooine hyperlane|hyperlane]] running from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the capital of the galaxy, to distant [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

[[File:Spero-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Master Gardener Spero, a native of Moltok living on Coruscant.]]
In [[300 BBY/Legends|300 BBY]],<ref name="EGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']].</ref> the arboreal Ho'Din began to [[Plague on Moltok|shift]] to a more industrial society. That required widespread clearing of Moltok's forests to make way for factories, cities,<ref name="UAA" /> [[Mining/Legends|mines]] and [[Farm/Legends|farms]]. As some species of flora became extinct, aggressive organisms on the forest floor were forced to adapt. Certain parasites from the lower levels found a new home within Ho'Din digestive tracts. The parasites took nourishment from the Ho'Din, causing them great suffering, eventually forcing the Ho'Din to withdraw back to the upper levels of the forests. After decades of research, the Ho'Din were able to overcome the parasite through herbal remedies; however, the experience had transformed the reptilian species. The Ho'Din subsequently worked hard to restore the natural habitats of their planet.<ref name="GG4" />

That restoration was supported by their dominant religion, [[Dinante Fli'R|&#91;Dinante Fli'R&#93;]]. It described the Ho'Din evolving from mobile plants and later being transformed into animals as retribution for their sins against nature. Nature was considered a passive force known as [[Dinegia|&#91;Dinegia&#93;]]. The religion further taught that if the Ho'Din acted as good stewards of their environment they would fulfill [[Flik'a kirki|&#91;Flik'a kirki&#93;]], or the "Virtuous Circle of Nature", and be reborn as plants. The priest of &#91;Dinante Fli'R&#93; became the main civic rulers of Moltok, and erased records of the advances in technology produced by Ho'Din in their strip-clearing years. They also ensured that what little technology was on the planet was strictly controlled.<ref name="GG4" /> Crumbling ruins of the old factories and cities were the only reminder of that time.<ref name="UAA" /> That repression led some Ho'Din to develop a fascination for technology.<ref name="GMR">{{GamerCite|3|The Smugglers Alliance}}.</ref> Some decades later, during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] of [[22 BBY/Legends|22]] to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Moltok fell within territory controlled by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], which sought to secede from the Galactic Republic.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

The focus on botanical sciences bore fruit for the inhabitants of Moltok, as they were able to export their herbal medicines to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="GG4" /> Ho'Din products included [[Distilled Water of Moltokian Camba-Fruit]],<ref name="COJ" /> [[Ho'Din-style veggie omelet]]s<ref name="Dex">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}.</ref> and [[Ho'Din herbal tea]]s.<ref name="CRO">''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]''.</ref> These strong exports, coupled with the minimal imports to the world, made it one of the richest planets in the galactic market. That wealth was frequently used to sponsor botanical projects on worlds struck by disasters, and to [[Terraforming/Legends|terraform]] other planets into "gardens" to enable other beings to commune with nature.<ref name="GG4" /> Moltok remained in control of successive factions of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], including as part of [[Oversector Outer]], [[Thrawn's confederation]], the [[Pentastar Alignment]], and [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Pellaeon's Empire]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Under the Empire, some Ho'Din transported rare plants back to Moltok for botanists to study in greenhouses.<ref name="LCOJ" /> The [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] finally gained control of the space around Moltok in [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]],<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Botanical studies continued under the New Republic, including a study simulating the life cycle of the [[winged-star]]s of [[Caluula/Legends|Caluula]].<ref name="TUF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''.</ref> In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], Moltok had a population of between one and ten million. However, the planet was soon a target for invasion by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], an extra-galactic species, during their initial invasion of the Outer Rim Territories. Moltok was [[Attack on the Moltok system|captured]] by the Yuuzhan Vong and remained occupied for the duration of the war. While liberated after the war, by [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], Moltok had come under the control of a resurgent [[Fel Empire]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

==Inhabitants==
===Ho'Din===
{{Quote|Ho'Din are not limited to their eyes and ears, princess. We never forget our friends.|Spero|<ref name="SEN">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]].</ref>}}
The Ho'Din were bipedal reptilians of green and yellow coloration, averaging between 2.5 and 3 meters in height. They had a lipless mouth, two bulging dark eyes, and their heads were topped with red and violet tresses that functioned as thermographic sensors. Ho'Din had four-fingered hands with suction pads that aided the arboreal sentients in climbing. The average Ho'Din lifespan was 120 years, reaching sexual maturity at age 30.<ref name="GG4" />

The &#91;Dinante Fli'R&#93; church was central to Ho'Din life. Its consent was required for Ho'Din marriage, and the priestesses played a key intermediary role in the reproductive process, transferring the "seed of life" from the [[Gender/Legends|male]] to the female in imitation of insect-facilitated pollination. [[Youngling/Legends|Younglings]] produced outside that ceremony were drugged and sacrificed to the organisms of the forest floor. [[Death/Legends|Dead]] of all ages were likewise deposited on the forest floor to nourish further life.<ref name="GG4" />

[[File:Makurth-square.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A [[Makurth/Legends|Makurth]], a saurian species from Moltok.]]
Many Ho'Din became botanists renowned throughout the galaxy, such as [[Master Gardener]] [[Spero]]<ref name="SE">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''.</ref> and the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plett]], who settled on [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]].<ref name="COJ" /> However, a number became radical environmentalists, using their skills in acts of eco-terrorism. These included [[Ort Hoogra-D'En]],<ref name="ND">[[No Disintegrations (West End Games)|''No Disintegrations'']].</ref> [[Maki Salak]],<ref name="CCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''.</ref> and [[Yansan]].<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''.</ref>

===Makurth===
The Makurth were bipedal [[Reptile/Legends|saurians]], covered in green scales and with four prominent curved horns on their heads. They were nocturnal creatures, prone to snorting and flaring their nostrils in order to intimidate opponents.<ref name="DB" /> The carnivores also had a terrifying scream that they uttered before entering combat. Makurth found frequent employment with the criminal syndicate [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] as bodyguards.<ref name="CCG" /> A notable Makurth was [[Fohargh]], who trained as a [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] at the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Academy]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. He was killed in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]] with the future [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]].<ref name="DB" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[Troy Denning]] created Moltok, and its sentient Ho'Din inhabitants, for ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', a sourcebook published by [[West End Games]] [[1989]]. The planet received mentions in several other West End Games publications before appearing as a planet in [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']], a [[LucasArts]] strategy game released in [[1998]]. Later that same year, [[Decipher]] added the Makurth as a second sentient species to the planet with the release of its [[Special Edition Limited]] set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]]. Several publications have subsequently mentioned the planet, with [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]]'s ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', published in [[2009]], providing details of the planet's history.
